indicator_definition: The gross nitrogen balance (GNB) on agricultural land estimates the nitrogen surplus in the soil, calculated as the difference between nitrogen inputs (mineral fertilisers, manure, atmospheric deposition, biological fixation and crop residues) and outputs (crops and grass harvested). It is expressed in kilograms of nitrogen per hectare of agricultural land.
rationale: Excess nitrogen in agricultural soils contributes to water pollution through nitrate leaching, greenhouse gas emissions and biodiversity loss. Reducing the nitrogen surplus is essential for sustainable agricultural practices that protect water bodies and the broader environment.
methodology_characteristics: Data are compiled by Eurostat from national agricultural statistics on fertiliser use, livestock numbers and crop production. The GNB methodology follows the OECD/Eurostat approach for nutrient balance calculation and is updated annually.
